name: Pembrolizumab (checkpoint immunotherapy, previously treated anal SCC)

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.histology: squamous cell carcinoma of the anus
biomarkers.note: Anti-PD-1 monotherapy is active in previously treated metastatic anal squamous cell carcinoma; MMR-deficient/MSI-high or high PD-L1 (CPS) status strengthens the case but is not required. Flat dosing is independent of body size. General reference: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) / DeVita.

premedications.name: None routine
premedications.notes: No routine premedication; manage infusion reactions if they occur.

supportiveCare: Pembrolizumab flat 200 mg IV every 3 weeks (or 400 mg IV every 6 weeks), continued until progression or unacceptable toxicity.
Counsel on immune-related adverse events and provide a wallet card; have a management pathway for endocrinopathy, colitis, pneumonitis, and hepatitis.
monitoring: thyroid, liver, renal function and glucose before dosing (immune-related toxicity surveillance)
symptom review for immune-related colitis, pneumonitis, dermatitis, endocrinopathy each visit

doseModificationRules.text: Hold pembrolizumab and start corticosteroids per immune-related toxicity guidance; permanently discontinue for most grade 3-4 events. Clinical review required.

drugs.name: Pembrolizumab
drugs.notes: Pembrolizumab flat 200 mg IV on day 1 of a 21-day cycle (alternative 400 mg IV every 6 weeks). Flat dose, not weight- or BSA-based. Nivolumab 240 mg every 2 weeks (or 480 mg every 4 weeks) is an equivalent anti-PD-1 alternative. General reference: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) / DeVita.
